metrology-001.question: Which correctly describes the principle of the scanning electron microscope (SEM)?
choices: A finely focused electron beam is scanned over the sample surface, and secondary electrons and other emissions are detected to observe surface shape
Crystal structure is examined from X-ray diffraction
Film thickness is measured from light interference
metrology-001.explanation: An SEM scans an electron beam over the sample surface and forms an image by detecting the secondary and backscattered electrons emitted. It can observe surface shape at higher magnification than an optical microscope. In semiconductor fabs, CD-SEMs, which measure pattern linewidths, are used for process control.

metrology-002.question: What is mainly measured by ellipsometry (spectroscopic ellipsometry)?
choices: The resistance when current is passed through the sample
The thickness and refractive index of thin films, obtained from changes in the polarization of reflected light
The mass spectrum of a sample sputtered by ions
metrology-002.explanation: Ellipsometry shines polarized light on a sample, measures how the polarization of the reflected light changes, and compares it with an optical model to determine the thickness and refractive index of thin films. Because it measures accurately without contact or damage, it is widely used to control the thickness of oxide and other films.

metrology-003.question: Which correctly describes SIMS (secondary ion mass spectrometry)?
choices: Elements are examined from characteristic X-rays emitted under an electron beam
Film thickness is measured from optical reflectance
The sample is sputtered with primary ions while the emitted secondary ions are mass-analyzed to determine the depth distribution of impurities
metrology-003.explanation: SIMS irradiates the sample with primary ions to sputter its surface little by little and mass-analyzes the emitted secondary ions. By measuring while sputtering, it determines the depth distribution (profile) of impurity concentration with high sensitivity. It is often used to evaluate ion implantation and diffusion, but it is a destructive analysis because it removes material.

metrology-004.question: What is mainly measured by the four-point probe method?
metrology-004.explanation: In the four-point probe method, four needles in a straight line contact the sample; current flows through the outer two and voltage is measured across the inner two. Separating the current and voltage probes allows sheet resistance to be measured without the influence of contact resistance. It is used to evaluate diffused layers and metal films.

metrology-005.question: Which correctly describes the sample preparation needed to observe a sample with a transmission electron microscope (TEM)?
choices: Stack samples to a thickness of several cm
Thin the sample to about 100 nm or less so electrons can pass through it
metrology-005.explanation: A TEM forms images from electrons that pass through the sample, so the sample must be very thin. For semiconductor devices, the area of interest is commonly cut into a thin lamella with a focused ion beam (FIB). Cross-sectional structures can then be observed at resolution high enough to see atomic arrangements.

metrology-006.question: Which is a typical principle used in defect inspection tools that detect particles and pattern defects on wafers?
choices: Detecting light scattered when light is shone on the wafer, and comparing images of adjacent dies
The sound when the wafer is tapped
metrology-006.explanation: Particles scatter incident light, so they are found by detecting scattered light. Pattern defects are detected by comparing the image with that of a neighboring die with the same pattern and flagging places that differ. Detected defects are then examined in detail with an SEM and classified (review).

metrology-007.question: What is mainly measured with an atomic force microscope (AFM)?
metrology-007.explanation: An AFM brings a sharp probe tip close to the sample surface and scans while detecting the deflection caused by atomic forces between tip and surface, measuring surface topography. It can measure height differences at the atomic level, so it is used for evaluating surface roughness after CMP and similar tasks.

metrology-008.question: What can be determined with EDX (energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy), used together with SEM and TEM?
choices: The kinds and amounts of elements in the sample
metrology-008.explanation: When an electron beam strikes a sample, characteristic X-rays with energies specific to each element are emitted. EDX analyzes those energies to determine the kinds and amounts of elements in the sample. Because it can analyze the composition of the spot observed under the electron microscope, it is widely used to analyze particles and defect sites.

metrology-009.question: Which method is often used to analyze trace metal contamination on wafer surfaces?
metrology-009.explanation: TXRF directs X-rays at the wafer surface at a very shallow angle so they are totally reflected, and measures the fluorescent X-rays from atoms near the surface. Because it analyzes only the surface with high sensitivity, it is used to control trace metal contamination on wafer surfaces, for example in evaluating cleaning steps.

metrology-010.question: Which can be evaluated from C-V (capacitance-voltage) measurements of a MOS capacitor?
choices: Oxide thickness, interface states, substrate doping concentration and more
The number of particles on the wafer surface
metrology-010.explanation: Measuring capacitance while varying the voltage applied to a MOS capacitor shows capacitance changing with the accumulation, depletion and inversion states. From the curve, oxide thickness, flat-band voltage, interface state density, substrate doping concentration and more can be evaluated. It is a basic technique for evaluating gate dielectric quality.

metrology-011.question: What is the measurement called that shines light on periodic patterns and compares the spectrum of reflected and diffracted light with a model to determine linewidth and cross-sectional shape?
metrology-011.explanation: Scatterometry measures the spectrum of light reflected and diffracted from periodic test patterns and matches it against spectra calculated from a shape model, determining linewidth, height, sidewall angle and more. Because it is fast and nondestructive, it is used for dimension control on production lines.

metrology-012.question: What can mainly be evaluated by X-ray diffraction (XRD)?
choices: Crystal structure, lattice constants and film strain
metrology-012.explanation: XRD determines crystal structure and lattice constants from the angles at which X-rays are diffracted by atomic planes in a crystal. It is used to evaluate the composition, strain and crystallinity of epitaxial films and similar properties.

metrology-013.question: What are the main uses of focused ion beam (FIB) systems?
choices: Machining tiny areas, preparing cross-section samples and modifying circuits
Measuring film thickness over the whole wafer
metrology-013.explanation: An FIB focuses ions such as gallium onto a sample to mill a target location with nanometer precision, or deposit films when combined with gases. It is used to prepare thin lamellae for TEM, observe cross-sections of defect sites, and modify the wiring of prototype chips.

metrology-014.question: Which analysis method determines surface elements and their chemical bonding states from the energies of photoelectrons emitted under X-ray irradiation?
metrology-014.explanation: XPS shines X-rays on the surface and measures the energies of the photoelectrons ejected, determining which elements are present and their chemical bonding states, such as whether they are oxidized. It gives information on the top few nm, so it is used to evaluate thin films, interfaces and surface treatments.

metrology-015.question: Which analysis technique locates failures in an LSI by detecting faint light emitted from defective sites during operation?
metrology-015.explanation: Sites where leakage current flows or transistors behave abnormally can emit very faint light. Emission microscopy detects this light with a highly sensitive camera to locate failures on the chip. Observation is sometimes done from the back of the chip.

metrology-016.question: When ArF resist patterns are measured with a CD-SEM, what is the phenomenon called in which electron-beam irradiation makes the patterns shrink?
choices: Shrinkage (resist shrinkage due to the electron beam)
metrology-016.explanation: ArF resist is sensitive to electron beams, and the irradiation used for measurement can break down molecules, reducing volume and shrinking the pattern. This causes measurement error, so measurements are made with measures such as reducing the electron dose.

metrology-017.question: What is placed on the wafer to measure overlay error?
metrology-017.explanation: To measure overlay accuracy, dedicated marks (targets) combining patterns from the previous and current layers are made in places such as the scribe lines around chips. Optical metrology tools measure their relative positions to determine the misalignment, which is also used to correct the exposure tool.

metrology-018.question: Which technique directs X-rays at a very shallow angle and determines thin-film thickness and density from oscillations in reflectivity?
metrology-018.explanation: XRR measures reflectivity while varying the angle of X-rays incident at shallow angles. X-rays reflected from the film surface and interface interfere, making reflectivity oscillate; thickness is obtained from the period, and density from the angle at which total reflection occurs. It is used to evaluate ultrathin films a few nm thick.

metrology-019.question: Which method is used to measure wafer bow, warp and flatness?
choices: Noncontact shape measurement with optical interferometers or capacitance sensors
metrology-019.explanation: Wafer shape is measured without contact, using instruments based on optical interference or sensors that measure the distance to both sides of the wafer by capacitance. Bow and flatness affect exposure focus and wafer handling and chucking, so they are controlled in incoming wafer inspection and after deposition.

metrology-020.question: Which technique evaluates whether a measuring instrument's repeatability and reproducibility are small enough compared with the process variation to be controlled?
metrology-020.explanation: Variation in measured values includes the variation of the measuring instrument as well as that of the process itself. Gage R&R evaluates variation when the same sample is measured repeatedly (repeatability) and when operators or tools are changed (reproducibility), to judge whether the instrument can be used for process control.

metrology-021.question: What is the main reason fine patterns a few tens of nm wide cannot be observed directly with an optical microscope?
choices: Because diffraction of light limits resolution (to roughly the wavelength of light)
Because optical microscopes show no color
Because optical microscopes are too dark
metrology-021.explanation: Because of diffraction, the resolution of an optical microscope is limited to about half the wavelength of the light used. Visible light has wavelengths of about 400–700 nm, so patterns a few tens of nm wide cannot be resolved. SEMs and TEMs, which use electron beams with shorter wavelengths, are therefore used.

metrology-022.question: Which equation is used to determine film stress from the change in wafer bow before and after deposition?
metrology-022.explanation: Stoney's equation gives film stress from the substrate thickness and elastic constants, the film thickness, and the change in wafer curvature before and after deposition. Stress is evaluated by measuring wafer bow with a laser or similar means. Black's equation concerns electromigration, and Preston's equation concerns CMP removal rate.

metrology-023.question: Whereas SIMS measures the atomic concentration of impurities, which method measures the depth distribution of electrically active carrier concentration?
choices: Electrical measurements such as spreading resistance profiling (SRP)
metrology-023.explanation: Spreading resistance profiling polishes the sample at an angle to stretch out the depth direction, then measures resistance with probes along it to obtain the depth distribution of carrier concentration. SIMS measures atomic concentration including inactive impurities, so comparing the two reveals how well the impurities have been activated.

metrology-024.question: What is the measurement called that monitors a process by measuring product wafers partway through processing on the production line?
metrology-024.explanation: Inline metrology uses measurement tools built into the production line to measure film thickness, dimensions, overlay, defects and more on product wafers during processing. It finds abnormalities early and keeps defective products from flowing to later steps. Nondestructive methods that do not damage the product are used.

metrology-025.question: Which inspection detects defects such as contact open failures using differences in brightness caused by differences in charging under an electron beam?
metrology-025.explanation: Under an electron beam, contacts electrically connected to the substrate and elsewhere let charge escape and appear bright (or dark), while floating contacts that are disconnected charge up and appear with a different brightness. This difference reveals open failures that cannot be seen from appearance.

metrology-026.question: When observing insulating samples with an SEM, which is a correct way to prevent charging (charge-up)?
choices: Lower the accelerating voltage, or coat the sample surface with a thin conductive film
Raise the accelerating voltage as high as possible
metrology-026.explanation: When an electron beam strikes an insulator, charge builds up instead of escaping, distorting the image and disturbing brightness. Charging is prevented by lowering the accelerating voltage to balance incoming and emitted electrons, coating the surface with a thin conductive film of gold or carbon, or observing under low-vacuum conditions.

metrology-027.question: Which technology is being researched and introduced to measure shapes such as deep holes three-dimensionally without cutting cross-sections?
choices: Visual inspection with an optical microscope
Dimension measurement using X-ray scattering (CD-SAXS) and similar methods
metrology-027.explanation: For deep, narrow structures such as 3D NAND memory holes, internal shapes are hard to see with optical metrology or SEMs, and cross-section observation is destructive. Because X-rays penetrate materials easily, methods such as CD-SAXS, which determines the shape of periodic structures from X-ray scattering patterns, are being researched and introduced.

metrology-028.question: Which method is used to measure interstitial oxygen concentration in silicon?
metrology-028.explanation: Interstitial oxygen in silicon absorbs infrared light at a specific wavenumber. Measuring the strength of that absorption by FTIR gives the oxygen concentration nondestructively. It is widely used to control the oxygen concentration of CZ wafers and also to measure carbon and other concentrations.

metrology-029.question: Which method measures wafer carrier lifetime without contact to evaluate metal contamination and the like?
metrology-029.explanation: In μ-PCD, a light pulse generates carriers in the wafer, and their decay through recombination is measured from changes in microwave reflection. Metal contamination shortens lifetime, so it is used to monitor contamination in furnaces and similar equipment.

metrology-030.question: Which function captures SEM images of defects found in inspection and automatically classifies their types from the images?
metrology-030.explanation: Defect inspection tools detect many defects, but investigating their causes requires classifying their types. ADC (Automatic Defect Classification) automatically sorts review SEM images into categories such as particles, pattern defects and scratches, speeding up root-cause identification. Machine learning has also been applied in recent years.

metrology-031.question: Which correctly describes the general difference between "metrology" and "inspection" on a semiconductor production line?
choices: Metrology measures values such as dimensions and film thickness, while inspection searches for abnormalities such as particles and pattern defects
Metrology and inspection mean exactly the same thing
Metrology is done only by eye and inspection only by tools
metrology-031.explanation: Production lines distinguish metrology, which quantitatively measures values such as line width, film thickness and overlay, from inspection, which finds abnormalities such as particles and missing or bridged patterns over wide areas. Both are done to learn the process state early and reduce defects.
choiceNotes: Correct. Metrology measures values; inspection searches for abnormalities.
Their purposes and tools differ.
Both are mainly done with dedicated tools.

metrology-032.question: What is the main purpose of performing metrology and inspection partway through the process on a production line?
choices: To deliberately slow down the process
To catch process abnormalities early and stop them, preventing large volumes of defective product
metrology-032.explanation: LSI manufacturing takes months, so discovering a problem only at the end would leave large volumes of defective product. Measuring and inspecting mid-process catches abnormalities early, so the responsible tool or step can be stopped and corrected, limiting losses.
choiceNotes: Slowing the process is not the purpose.
Correct. It catches abnormalities early to limit losses.
It is not to increase weight.

metrology-033.question: In production-line metrology, why are only selected wafers or points often measured rather than all of them?
choices: Because measuring everything would destroy the product
Because metrology tools can be used only once a day
Because metrology costs time and money, samples are measured to the extent needed to understand process variation
metrology-033.explanation: Metrology consumes tool time and cost, and measuring every point on every wafer would slow production. Measurements therefore follow a sampling plan that sets how many wafers per lot and how many points per wafer to measure, matched to the nature of process variation.
choiceNotes: Most metrology is non-destructive and does not damage product.
Metrology tools can be used continuously.
Correct. Samples are measured with time and cost in mind.

metrology-034.question: Which correctly describes observing a cross-section in detail after breaking or milling the wafer?
choices: Only surface contamination can be seen
It is destructive, so the observed wafer or chip cannot be used as product
The product can be shipped as is
metrology-034.explanation: Cross-sectional SEM or TEM observation breaks the wafer or mills it with FIB, so the observed area can no longer be used as product (destructive analysis). Samples are therefore pulled from production wafers or dedicated evaluation wafers are used.
choiceNotes: Cross-sectional structure can be examined in detail.
Correct. It is destructive and cannot become product.
Broken or milled wafers cannot be shipped.

metrology-035.question: Which pair correctly names a measuring instrument's property of "small spread when measuring the same thing repeatedly" and that of "measured values being close to the true value"?
metrology-035.explanation: Small spread on repeated measurements is called precision, and closeness of measured values to the true value is called accuracy. Even with small spread, measurements offset from the true value are not accurate. Calibration and reference standards are used to manage both.
choiceNotes: Sensitivity and resolution are different properties.
Speed and capacity are not metrology accuracy terms.
Correct. Precision (spread) and accuracy (closeness to truth).

metrology-036.question: Which spectroscopic method is often used to evaluate stress (strain) in silicon locally and non-destructively?
metrology-036.explanation: Raman spectroscopy measures light scattered with a slight wavelength shift due to interaction with lattice vibrations when a laser is applied (Raman scattering). Stress in silicon changes this shift (the Raman shift), so strain in transistor channels and stress from packaging can be evaluated locally.
choiceNotes: Correct. Stress is evaluated from the Raman shift.
The four-point probe measures resistivity.
C-V measurement measures the capacitance of MOS structures.

metrology-037.question: Which method is used to observe solder joint voids and wire shapes inside a package in three dimensions without destroying it?
metrology-037.explanation: X-ray CT captures X-ray transmission images from many directions and computationally reconstructs a 3D image of the interior. Without destroying the package, voids and bridges in BGA solder balls, wire deformation and internal cracks can be observed.
choiceNotes: Ellipsometry measures thin-film thickness and optical constants.
SIMS is a destructive method that analyzes elements while sputtering the sample.
Correct. The interior is reconstructed in 3D from X-ray transmission images.

metrology-038.question: Which tool is widely used to find delamination at interfaces inside a package, such as between molding compound and chip, non-destructively?
metrology-038.explanation: A scanning acoustic microscope (SAT) applies ultrasound to the package in water and images the waves reflected from internal interfaces. At delaminated areas, the air gap reflects sound strongly, so delamination between resin and chip or leadframe, cracks and voids can be found non-destructively.
choiceNotes: Correct. Delamination is found from ultrasonic reflections.
An electron-beam writer draws patterns.
An ion implanter introduces impurities.

metrology-039.question: Which method evaluates the quality of compound semiconductor wafers and epi layers without contact by shining laser light and measuring the spectrum and intensity distribution of the emitted light?
metrology-039.explanation: Photoluminescence creates carriers with laser light above the band gap and measures the light emitted when they recombine. The emission wavelength reveals composition and band gap, and the intensity distribution reveals defects and non-uniformity, so it is widely used to evaluate epi layers for LEDs and lasers.
choiceNotes: AFM measures surface topography.
Correct. It measures light emitted under illumination.
The four-point probe is a contact method for resistivity.

metrology-040.question: Compared with bright-field wafer inspection, which images patterns directly, what characterizes dark-field inspection, which captures only scattered light?
choices: It detects scattered light from particles and the like with high sensitivity and readily inspects large areas at high speed
It always has higher resolution than bright field
metrology-040.explanation: Dark-field inspection rejects specularly reflected light and captures only light scattered by particles and defects, so small particles appear bright against a dark background and inspection is fast. Bright-field inspection images patterns directly with reflected light and excels at finding pattern-shape defects. The two are used according to purpose.
choiceNotes: Correct. Scattered light enables sensitive, fast particle detection.
For pattern-shape defects, bright field can be superior.
Dark field is well suited to detecting particles.

metrology-041.question: Which instrument traces a sample surface with a fine stylus and measures step heights and surface shape from the stylus's vertical motion?
metrology-041.explanation: A stylus profiler traces the surface with a fine-tipped stylus at constant force and measures step heights and surface waviness from its vertical displacement. It is used to check etch depth, film steps and post-CMP planarity. It covers a wider range than AFM, scanning over millimeters.
choiceNotes: A mass spectrometer identifies components from ion masses.
Correct. It traces the surface with a stylus to measure steps.
An ellipsometer measures film thickness from changes in polarization.

metrology-042.question: What is the technique called that uses statistical models to predict film thickness or dimensions of wafers that were not actually measured, from equipment sensor data and the like?
metrology-042.explanation: Virtual metrology models the relationship between a tool's sensor data during processing (temperature, pressure, power and so on) and past measurement results, using machine learning or similar, to predict results for unmeasured wafers. It estimates the process state without measuring every wafer, helping with early anomaly detection and control.
choiceNotes: Destructive analysis examines samples by breaking them.
Visual inspection looks for abnormalities in appearance.
Correct. It predicts measurements from sensor data.

metrology-043.question: When measuring very narrow trenches or steep sidewalls with AFM, what tends to cause errors?
choices: AFM can only be used in vacuum
The tip has a finite size and shape, so its shape gets superimposed on the measured profile
metrology-043.explanation: AFM measures shape by tracing the surface with a tip, so it cannot reach the bottoms of trenches narrower than the tip, and on steep sidewalls the side of the tip makes contact first. The measured profile is therefore a convolution of the actual shape with the tip shape. Sharper tips and analysis that corrects for tip shape are used.
choiceNotes: AFM can also be used in air.
Correct. The tip's shape is superimposed on the result.
AFM is an instrument for measuring surface topography.

metrology-044.question: In TEM, which technique scans a finely focused electron beam and measures the energy lost by transmitted electrons to map elements and chemical states?
metrology-044.explanation: In STEM (scanning transmission electron microscopy), a fine electron beam is scanned across the sample. Combined with EELS, which measures how much energy transmitted electrons lose, element types and chemical bonding states can be mapped with near-atomic spatial resolution. It is used to evaluate ultra-thin gate insulators and interfaces.
choiceNotes: The four-point probe measures resistivity.
Hall measurement determines carrier type, concentration and mobility.
Correct. Elements and states are probed by the energy loss of transmitted electrons.

metrology-045.question: Which analysis method field-evaporates atoms one by one from the tip of a needle-shaped specimen and detects their positions and identities to map the 3D distribution of atoms such as dopants?
metrology-045.explanation: In an atom probe, a specimen shaped into a needle by FIB is subjected to high voltage and pulses so that tip atoms leave one at a time as ions; their arrival positions and times at the detector reveal element types and original positions. The 3D distribution of dopants inside transistors and similar can be examined at the atomic level.
choiceNotes: Correct. Atoms are removed one by one to map their 3D distribution.
Optical microscopes cannot show atomic distributions.
Acoustic microscopes examine delamination inside packages and the like.

metrology-046.question: Which method, without forming electrodes, deposits charge on the wafer surface by corona discharge and measures changes in surface potential to evaluate oxide and interface electrical properties?
choices: Contactless electrical evaluation using corona charging (such as COCOS)
metrology-046.explanation: Depositing charge on the wafer by corona discharge and measuring surface potential contactlessly with a Kelvin probe allows oxide thickness, charge, interface states, leakage and more to be evaluated without building MOS structures. Because no gate electrode is needed, it is used for in-line monitoring.
choiceNotes: The four-point probe is a contact method for resistivity.
X-ray diffraction examines crystal structure.
Correct. Corona charging and surface potential measurement are used.

metrology-047.question: Which technique locates faults by detecting tiny heat generation in a powered chip with high sensitivity, periodically modulating the applied power and accumulating synchronized thermal images?
metrology-047.explanation: Lock-in thermography switches the voltage applied to the chip on and off at a fixed period and accumulates only the infrared thermal images synchronized with that period, detecting the location of very slight heating from shorts and the like. Because it can narrow down fault locations even from outside the package, it is used early in failure analysis.
choiceNotes: Correct. Synchronized thermal images detect tiny heating.
Ellipsometry measures film thickness.
SIMS profiles elements in depth.

metrology-048.question: Which method sends fast pulses into package or board wiring and determines the location of opens or shorts from the reflected waveforms?
metrology-048.explanation: TDR injects a fast-rising pulse into a wire and measures the timing and shape of signals reflected where impedance changes. The return time gives the distance and the waveform shows whether it is an open or a short, so it is used to locate package defects.
choiceNotes: XPS examines surface elements and chemical states.
Correct. Defect locations are found from reflected waves.
AFM measures surface topography.

metrology-049.question: In optical defect inspection, why does detection become sharply harder as particles get smaller?
choices: The scattering intensity of particles much smaller than the wavelength falls steeply, roughly with the sixth power of particle size
Small particles do not reflect light
metrology-049.explanation: Light scattering by particles much smaller than the wavelength (Rayleigh scattering) has an intensity proportional to roughly the sixth power of particle size. Halving the size reduces scattered light to about 1/64, burying it in background noise from the surface. Shorter wavelengths and complementary electron-beam inspection are therefore used.
choiceNotes: Correct. Scattered light falls with roughly the sixth power of size.
Small particles still scatter light, but much more weakly.
Particles do not become transparent.

metrology-050.question: What is the approach called that combines data from multiple measurement methods (optical, CD-SEM, AFM and so on) to determine dimensions and shapes more accurately than any single method?
metrology-050.explanation: For leading-edge fine structures, any single method is limited in what it can measure and how precisely. Hybrid metrology feeds values measured accurately by one method (such as film thickness) into another method's analysis model and so on, so the methods compensate for each other's weaknesses and give more accurate results.
choiceNotes: This is not a common metrology approach by that name.
Correct. It combines methods to improve accuracy.
This is not a common metrology approach by that name.
